title: Sri Lankan Chicken Curry
subtitle: Coconut milk chicken curry with roasted spices
excerpt: Sri Lankan chicken curry is darker and more complex than many Indian versions because the spices are often dry-roasted before grinding. Coconut milk gives it a rich, silky sauce. Curry leaves and cinnamon are the defining flavours.
sourceNotes: Sri Lankan curry differs from South Indian curry in its use of roasted or dark-roasted spice blends. Coconut milk, curry leaves, and pandan leaf appear across the island's cooking. The dish varies between the Sinhalese, Tamil, and Burgher communities.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the coconut milk. Add coconut milk when reheating.

content.text: Bone-in chicken thighs give the best flavour here. If using boneless, reduce the cooking time by 5 minutes and check earlier. The curry leaves fry in hot oil at the start -- this is important for their flavour.

items.prepNote: use a 400ml tin of coconut milk
use 8 fresh curry leaves if available

content.text: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the curry leaves and cloves. Fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the onion. Cook for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the turmeric, cinnamon, and chilli flakes. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the chicken pieces and brown on all sides for 5 minutes. Season with salt.
Pour in the coconut milk and 100ml of water. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove the lid and cook for 5 more minutes to thicken the sauce slightly. Taste and adjust salt. Serve with rice.

items.cause: Too much heat after adding the coconut milk
items.fix: Always simmer gently -- do not boil hard once the coconut milk is in

items.cause: Coconut milk is rich and sweet; not enough spice to balance
items.fix: Add a pinch more chilli flakes and a squeeze of lemon juice to balance

items.cause: Not browned well enough at the start
items.fix: Brown the chicken in batches over high heat; the skin should crisp before the coconut milk is added

content.text: Sri Lanka sits at the tip of India and its cooking shares ingredients with South India while going its own way. Roasted spice blends, coconut milk, and curry leaves define the island's flavour profile. Chicken curry is eaten for lunch and dinner across all communities and is the dish most visitors encounter first.
